title: ～やすい — easy to ～, tends to ～
summary: Added to a verb to mean “easy to ～” or “apt to ～.” It attaches to the stem (ます-form without ます). The whole thing then behaves like an い-adjective. The opposite is ～にくい or ～づらい.

patterns.form: 動詞ます形（語幹） ＋ やすい
patterns.gloss: stem + やすい (読む → 読みやすい)

body.p: The first is “easy to do because of the nature of the thing”: 読みやすい本, 分かりやすい説明. The second is a tendency, often an unwelcome one: 事故が起きやすい (accidents tend to happen), 風邪をひきやすい (catch a cold easily).
Because it ends in い, it conjugates as an い-adjective: 読みやすかった, 読みやすくない, 読みやすくて. It can modify a noun directly: 読みやすい本.

examples.ja: この本（ほん）は字（じ）が大（おお）きくて読（よ）みやすいです。
examples.romaji: Kono hon wa ji ga ōkikute yomiyasui desu.
examples.tr: This book has big letters and is easy to read.

examples.ja: 先生（せんせい）の話（はなし）はとても分（わ）かりやすいです。
examples.romaji: Sensei no hanashi wa totemo wakariyasui desu.
examples.tr: The teacher's explanations are very easy to understand.

examples.ja: この道（みち）は暗（くら）くて、事故（じこ）が起（お）きやすい。
examples.romaji: Kono michi wa kurakute, jiko ga okiyasui.
examples.tr: This road is dark and accidents tend to happen easily.

pitfalls: Use the stem: 読みやすい, not 読むやすい.
The thing that is easy to do is the subject: この本は読みやすい. The subject is not the person who reads.
